step1_analysis.description: A passive LC network acting as a resonator, likely used as the switched resonator load for the dual-band LNA mentioned in the paper. It consists of inductors with series loss resistances and parallel tuning/parasitic capacitors.

paper_reference.title: A Dual-Band CMOS Front-End With Two Gain Modes for Wireless LAN Applications

f_res.description: Primary resonant frequency where the impedance magnitude is maximized.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the LC product of the tank components. f_res ≈ 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L_eq * C_eq)).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper targets the 2.4 GHz ISM and 5.15 GHz UNII bands. The passive component values would be sized to resonate at these frequencies.

Z_max.description: Peak impedance magnitude at the resonant frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Z_max ≈ Q * sqrt(L/C) or Rp = (L / (C * Rs)).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical on-chip LC tanks have a parallel equivalent resistance in the range of a few hundred ohms due to inductor Q-factors of 5 to 15.

Q_factor.description: Quality factor of the resonator at the resonant frequency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: On-chip spiral inductors in standard CMOS processes typically exhibit Q factors between 5 and 15 at low GHz frequencies.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the impedance profile of the 1-port LC resonator to find its resonant frequency, peak impedance, and quality factor.
